texts.text: The pile that fell from the sky turns out to be corpses, mangled beyond all recognition. A curious golden glow, bright like sunlight, winks through the gaps between the bodies.
The people I assume to be the "customers" mentioned in the announcement are desperately scrambling among the corpses, snatching up whatever they could find.

texts.speaker: Impatient Customer
texts.text: That way... Maybe there's more to gather over there...? Dammit, I took the wrong spot!

texts.speaker: Desperate Customer
texts.text: This spot is mine. Fuck off!

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: Whoa, you're a prickly one, aren'tcha. Fine, fine~ we'll back off~

texts.speaker: Destitute Customer
texts.text: Hey! Lift your foot. Didn't you just step on an eyeball?!

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: ... Uh, are you talking to me?

texts.speaker: Destitute Customer
texts.text: Did I see that wrong...? Whatever. Stop skulking around, then! You're throwing me off!

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: ... Hey, don't you think you should apologize if you got the wrong idea? *sigh* Actually, never mind.
I can see something twinkling there, but this probably isn't the right time to worry about that.
<color=#E1B643>.......</color>
A soft and warm peal of laughter brushes past the fingertips laid against the wall.
A pale light, reminiscent of the Golden Bough, glimmers beneath its surface.
A wall patched over with Golden Hide.
The presence is faint, but something about it feels like the Golden Bough.

texts.speaker: Treatment Customer
texts.text: Thank goodness I booked my dermal perm before the trend died! Once they layer the curl into every ridge of my skin, nobody will be able to tear their eyes away from me!

texts.speaker: Eye-shopping Customer
texts.text: Got any empty bottles left? A spare palm would do, too.

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: I... don't think we have any empty bottles or... spare palms... Sorry... ha... ha...

texts.speaker: Eye-shopping Customer
texts.text: Damn. I don't have enough eyeballs for this season's new collection...
The customer gnaws anxiously at their fingernails.
The label reads: "Coverage That Never Fades! Feel the Refreshing Lymph of Freshly Shed Skin! Instant Sellout!"
... It seems unnecessary to inspect the product itself.

texts.speaker: Yi Sang
texts.text: Dante. I am well aware that circumstances weigh heavily upon us... But ought we not hasten to find Meursault?

texts.speaker: Faust
texts.text: No further explanation from my side is necessary.

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: Was there something else you needed to check? Let's make it quick and get moving. We need to find Meursault ASAP.

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: *puff* Can't exactly take a proper break when I know one of us could be experiencing the worst thing out there. Let's go if you fellas are all rested up.

texts.speaker: Hong Lu
texts.text: Do you suppose Meursault is all right? Being cast out into a strange place like this, all on your own... It'd leave anyone terribly lost and afraid.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <I... don't think he'd feel lost and afraid... But yeah, best we hurry up and find him.>

texts.speaker: Hong Lu
texts.text: Fuhu... Then let's be on our way!
Sinclair is still huffing, apparently not yet over his anger.

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: Um... Manager... Shouldn't we hurry and start looking for Meursault?

texts.speaker: Don Quixote
texts.text: Hath the time arrived for us to resume our adventure? Verily, I remain ever at the ready!

texts.speaker: Heathcliff
texts.text: Bloody hell...
Heathcliff is pacing back and forth restlessly.

texts.speaker: Heathcliff
texts.text: Oh. Are we movin' again, then?

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: Please rest more if you remain fatigued, Executive Manager. Give the order, and I, Outis, shall detach a search party and...

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <It's okay. I should go with you guys.>

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: As expected of our Executive Manager. You are an example to every unit under your command...
Outis showers me with praise. Didn't know public restrooms came with showers.

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: We ready to go? Man, I sure hope we won't see another pile of corpses fallin' down on us. I don't wanna get crushed to death under a pile of rotting meat... That'd be the stuff of 3 nights-long-nightmare.

texts.speaker: Ryōshū
texts.text: G.G., C.H.
Gotta Go, Chore Hour? Or... Get Going, Clockhead...?
I'll go and ask Sinclair later.
*knock* *knock*

texts.speaker: Hong Lu
texts.text: Hello? Is anybody in~?

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <The door's locked... Is there nobody inside?>

texts.speaker: Ryōshū
texts.text: Clock. M.Y.H.

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: Clock, move your head, she says... Eep!
Ryōshū's scabbard rattles menacingly, swinging in Sinclair's direction.
It seems Araya has fallen into this peculiar space alongside us.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <We should probably check somewhere else first.>

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: Hm... It's not even budging.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: Did you not hear what I said? The door's not budging.

texts.speaker: Heathcliff
texts.text: *yawn*

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Heathcliff... I think she's talking to you.>

texts.speaker: Heathcliff
texts.text: ... The door won't budge, yeah. What do you want me to do about it?

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: What an absurd question. An obstacle emerges—you and that bat of yours terminate it without any thought given to the risk involved or the tactics available. Isn't that supposed to be your day-to-day doctrine of action?

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: The location beyond is yet to be screened, Executive Manager. Please fall back to a defensible distance. Heathcliff shall breach the door and scout ahead.

texts.speaker: Heathcliff
texts.text: Bloody hell, you've got some nerve telling me to put that door in! One look round and you can tell they spent a fortune on this place... What if they make us foot the bill after I've smashed it to bits?

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: Hm. You make a valid point. As the man says, Executive Manager. Reconnaissance beyond this door should be postponed...
Heathcliff stood agape at Outis, who didn't seem to feel even an ounce of hesitation about using him as cannon fodder. He stepped back, shaking his head as though the interaction had tired him out.

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: ... Are you planning to knock on the stalls all day, Dante?

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <You never know...>

texts.speaker: Hong Lu
texts.text: It's only proper to do so in a restroom. Toilet etiquette is an important virtue!

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: All well and good, I suppose... But shouldn't we be on our way and take a look around outside?

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <That's the plan.>

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: What's got you rattled, Manager Bud?

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <I just heard what sounded like a toilet flushing in there...>

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: ... You're still trying to spook me, even after everything we've been through? Not falling for it anymore... Nope...

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <But I really heard it...>

texts.speaker: Heathcliff
texts.text: Enough, Clockhead! What d'you reckon gawping inside those toilet stalls is going to do?

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: The Executive Manager is executing a methodical search pattern! Even these fixtures may conceal hints of intelligence decisive to the operation!

texts.speaker: Ryōshū
texts.text: *puff* This master detective inspected this entire restroom the moment we entered. There is nothing left to see, C.H.

texts.speaker: Hong Lu
texts.text: This reminds me of when we played detective back in T Corp.~ We had so much fun back then, didn't we, Rodya?

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: Yeah... we did. Anyway, how about we hurry up and get out of here first?
Yeah. We can't waste any more time here.
A stall with a closed door.
... (She gazes at me without a word. The serene smile on her face suggests that she regards us favorably.)

parts.notes: Can you tell us where we are again?

texts.text: ... It's the restroom.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Right...>

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Hang on... She can interpret my ticking?!>
... (She says nothing more, but her smile lingers still.>

parts.notes: What is your relationship with Demian?

texts.text: ... Keep following the star, then someday...

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: ... Star...
Sinclair seems to sink inward, lost in deep thought.

parts.notes: What kind of being are you?

texts.text: (She does not reply. It seems any attempt to uncover her identity will prove futile.)
A burning clock head comes into view. Neither the clothing nor the hands of the clock differ from their usual state.
Familiar golden light leaks through a narrow gap between the tiles.
I can almost hear the faint murmuring of conversation between people.
I peer through the gap, but the glare of the light is too bright for me to see anything.

texts.speaker: Treatment Customer
texts.text: Strangers—stop checking me out. I'm halfway through my makeover treatment. You couldn't tell who I was even if you tried.

texts.speaker: Treatment Customer
texts.text: *sigh* I just can't with these bums who can't even afford these treatments. Shoo. Scram. Mind your own business.

texts.speaker: Treatment Customer
texts.text: Stop staring at me!

texts.speaker: Treatment Customer
texts.text: Stop staring at me, I said!

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <And what's this?>

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: Looks like a salon heat lamp. I've seen a few before.

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: I remember spending hours sitting under one, trying to straighten my hair. It... didn't work, obviously.
Ishmael called it a salon heat lamp. I doubt it would do anything beyond warming my head.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... What even is this?>

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: I think it's... moving. Like twitching... And it's got those creepy knots tangled all over...

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: Let's not look too closely.
An unidentified display piece. ... Let's not look too closely.

markers.notes: Fount (After sinners returned to Fount, before finding Meursault)

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Guys, what happened?>

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: We can't leave the restroom. Heathcliff and Don Quixote both tried pretty much everything, but... nothing worked.

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: That's... a serious problem. It might mean we're the only ones allowed to go out.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: There has to be a way to circumvent this.
Four Sinners... on each floor...
... time... beyond that... cannot protect...

texts.speaker: Heathcliff
texts.text: Argh! Can't you finish a bloody sentence?! What's that even mean?!

texts.speaker: Yi Sang
texts.text: The meaning she seeks to convey appears to be that only four may exit the restroom simultaneously. Perhaps any number greater than that poses a certain risk.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Okay... Isn't it still three, though? Counting me?>

texts.speaker: Faust
texts.text: Counting Meursault, who is currently not present in the restroom, the number adds up to four.

texts.speaker: Hong Lu
texts.text: Oh, you're right. Hmm... Is there a way to change who is allowed out then, I wonder?

texts.speaker: Don Quixote
texts.text: I am afraid not, young Hong Lu. I harbored much the selfsame suspicion as thee, and had sought to depart moments after young Ishmael and Rodya's return... Alas, the door permitted not my passing.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: Four Sinners on each floor. That's what she said.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: And, if I were to hazard a guess... the roster cannot be altered once it has been finalized. Am I correct?
She nodded lightly at Outis's conjecture before adding another comment.
... can... change... when floors... change...

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: ... Can't be helped, I suppose. Let's the three of us head out for now.

texts.speaker: Yi Sang
texts.text: Mm. Remain vigilant, dear fellows.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Time to go find Meursault.>

markers.notes: Attempting to cross the barrier before it unlocks.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <It looks like an ordinary belt barrier. I should be able to step right over it... But the second I try, it feels impossible.>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: That is because we are currently in the Symbolic.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: Physically, the object consists only of two metal posts joined by a retractable belt. However, it has been assigned the symbolic function of denying passage.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: That function is absolute as far as its symbolic meaning is concerned. It cannot be crossed within this realm, Manager.

texts.speaker: Yi Sang
texts.text: This place is quiet to an uncanny degree. A "room of rest"... Truly, a chamber wherein one may rest freely.
Faust is staring into the empty space.

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: Ready when you are.

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: If this is how it's gonna be... Well, I'll need a smoke.
I turn my head and see Ryōshū with a cigarette already pinched between her teeth, a wisp of smoke rising from the tip.
Hong Lu seems to be listening to whatever story Don Quixote's telling with genuine delight.
Sinclair is bombarding the blue lady with all kind of questions.
I don't think the conversation is going particularly well.
Don Quixote is recounting the acts and miracles of Fixers animatedly, in an effort to keep everyone's mood alight.
... Hong Lu seems to be the only one paying attention.
Heathcliff keeps circling the same spot restlessly.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: It is rather frustrating that I am unable to be of assistance, trapped in this location. Should you need me, Executive Manager, I, Outis, am ready to be of service at your command.

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: I'll be restin' here for a bit. Gimme a shout when it's time to leave~
Ryōshū has her eyes closed. The sizzle and hiss from the tip of the cigarette, however, tells me that she's not asleep.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: I am ready, Manager.

texts.speaker: Eye-shopping Customer
texts.text: This trend had better die soon. I don't have a single patch of bare skin left for another polka dot.

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: Ooh, another eyeball!

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: Whoa, you were a blur. You've got fast hands, huh.
We picked up an eyeball dropped by a customer.

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: What's all that?

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: Clothes that have fallen out of fashion due to the passing of the trend seasons.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: Someone has gathered them here.

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: They're tucked away in such an out-of-the-way corner. It almost seems like someone was trying to hide them away...

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: Ya know how fashion is—it's one big cycle. Maybe somebody stashed 'em here until they can come back in style?

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Could these be items for sale?>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: There is very little evidence to support that possibility. They lack proper price tags and have not been maintained, Manager.

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: Hup...! Aww. No dice. Figures...

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: W-what are you doing?

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: I'm tryin' to take one, obviously. Sorry, Meur, but can ya grab whichever one's in the best shape? There's a bunch of other stuff there mixed in with the clothes, too.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: ... Understood.
Obtained 10 eyeballs.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Why would they display it in such a... contorted pose?>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: To present the upper and lower body, including the head and feet, simultaneously in the customer's field of vision.

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: ... But why? Just keep it standing upright, and people'll just look up and down to check it out.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: That would—

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: Why go through the effort, Ishy? This way, the whole outfit fits neatly into view~

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: ... That's what you were about to say, right, Meur?

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: Correct.
Ishmael slowly nodded as if she had finally accepted that this place operated on a common sense all its own.
Mannequins stand on display.

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: Ugh... Its eyes are followin' us whenever we move.

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: Those ones gave us a once-over, then turned their heads away.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: Their expressions suggested that the sight of us exceeded their tolerance for the visually objectionable.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Wow. That's kind of hurtful...>
What looks like a department-store directory is glued on a drink vending machine. Damage has obscured most of the lettering.

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: ... Hey, what's up with this map? Looks a bit weird to me...

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: You're right... According to the diagram, the department store should be far larger and more complicated than what we've seen.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: The map is unlikely to be erroneous. This department store occupies an immense spatial domain; the locations accessible to our perception likely constitute only a minute fraction of the whole.

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: And this place is supposed to hold... 300 million people, huh?

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: Oh, does it say which floor has the Golden Bough?

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: Why would anyone put that in the directory?

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: Hey, you never know...
Maybe I really was a tree in a past life.
When I encountered the diagram and structure of the mind in arboreal form...
... I felt drawn toward it and concluded it to be the rendering of the soul.
But I wonder... does the soul really take the shape of a tree?
Perhaps a tree is merely one way of representing it. The mind may be too unstable to possess a ■■■■■ ■■■■■■■■■ at all.
Yet, the human forms I saw the ■■■■■ shape throughout the City converge again and again upon the structure of a tree.
The blueprint for ■ ■■■■.'■ ■■■■■■■ System alone suggests as much, does it not?

markers.notes: Returning to the Fount before finding Meursault.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Well, we made it back, at least...>

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: Executive Manager. Are you able to see Meursault's present surroundings? I recall you awakened a highly convenient ability in an effort to assist the more lacking members of our team.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: If anything is visible, I propose we use those details to locate the site where he is being detained.

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: Oh, right. You could do that, couldn't you, Manager Bud? If you can spot anything from his end, that oughta narrow the search down and make things easier for us.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Hmm... I don't know if it'll work from here, but I'll give it a try.>

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <I think I see... uh, a carpeted floor? Yeah, that's carpet... and there are strips of fabric up ahead... Clothes, probably. Looks like they've got them on display. Meursault's standing absolutely still.>

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <He doesn't seem to be tied up or anything... Huh? There's someone beside him...>

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: Tch. Not much time has passed since the execution, and he already allows himself to be taken captive. An uncharacteristic display of incompetence coming from him—and on multiple fronts.

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: Huh... Carpet, and clothes on display... Well, it's more than we had to go on before, at least.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <He doesn't look to be injured or in any immediate danger... Let's start by finding a carpeted room with clothes on display.>
Once, a child descended from a ■■■■ and rained down as water.
Water that gives the mind material form. ■■■■■■.
The experiments conducted ■■■■■ ■■■■■■ gave me the certainty:
The tree bears ten fruits.
The tree is divided into three domains.
And the order in which the tree ■■ ■■■ended carries significance.

markers.name: Annette
markers.notes: Scissors cost 10000 prior to completing Annette's request.
Available after Flannel and Felt's quest.
Obtained when answering 3F Floor Manager's question correctly or killing it.
Obtained from 'Well-sharpened Sewing Scissors' after using it on Two-piece.
Obtained after completing Flannel and Felt's quest.
Obtained when speaking to Annette with the 'Golden Skein'.
Obtained when interacting with L'Inamovible after defeating her.

texts.text:
[Differential of Falling Series 3: "Stockmann"
This installation was inspired by a Mannequin's fall through the Grand Magasin. The imagery evokes the falling continuity of time.
Sculpted in a smaller size relative to the Series 1 installation.]

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: I fail to see why anyone would put something like this on display and call it art.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: Though I cannot say what that woman, with her fixation on such bizarre aesthetics, might have thought of it...

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Hmm... you're right. If Ryōshū were here, she'd...>

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: Ryōshū... I think she'd call this D.R.A.B.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Drab? Oh... D.R.A.B. Acronym, huh?>

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: Yup. "Dull. Repetitive. Artless. Boring." ... That's probably how she'd see all of this.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: This is more than mere interpretation... You might as well be forming a genuine psychic link with her.
It occurred to me that Sinclair's progress was becoming more frightening by the day.

[Differential of Falling Series 1: "Cynthia"
This installation depicts the fall of Cynthia, the first Mannequin to fall in the Grand Magasin. The only large-scale installation in the series, it sets itself apart from the rest of the series by being the only piece to depict the precise moment her fall began in painstaking detail.]

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: Reminds me of the things we saw back at the Ring Nursefather's gallery.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: artistic about these things.>

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: Ah. There's something lying over there, though. Is that part of the... artwork too?

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <I don't think so. Can you grab that for me, Meursault?>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: It is within reach. These appear to be eyeballs. I will hold on to it for the time being.
It's a cash register. Reaching into its drawer to see if there's anything left... yields some eyeballs that were rolling around in its corner.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: Not a bad get, Executive Manager. Take it—it should do us good to find and keep as many of these as we can.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Uh... Are you sure?>

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: W-wait, isn't this just straight-up thievery?

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: A more accurate designation for this strategy would be "field requisition tactics."
<color=#ebcaa2>I don't know, this strategy probably falls under the designation we call "larceny" here.</color>

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: ... *cough*

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: <Wait, we're not allowed to take eyeballs from cash registers? What about all those Mannequins we kill—I mean, "helped to the exit"?>
<color=#ebcaa2>Fuhu, you mean "criminal damage to property"?</color>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: There are no criminal designations or legal framework for punishment for such behavior in the Grand Magasin, Manager.
<color=#ebcaa2>*scoff* You're no fun. Why would you tell them that?</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>Take it. It doesn't belong to anyone, anyway.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>And you...</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>Still haven't figured out jokes, have you?</color>
..."Field requisitioned" some eyeballs.
Don't need these that badly.
There isn't anything left.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Anybody know what this is...? Must have something to do with broadcasting since we're in the PA room.>

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: This appears to be a form of manual communication switchboard, Executive Manager.

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: What's a communication switchboard?

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: A device used to manage and connect circuits of telephones.

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: I've never seen anything like this... So phones used to have to go through these to connect?

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: These have mostly gone out of use nowadays. I've not seen one in a long time myself, in fact. Used to have a similar device back in... the CCC, or the Command and Control Center.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: Wired access via the manual switchboard allows for a much more stable connection as long as the wires are intact, meaning that it maintains operational capacity even in adverse communication conditions caused by devices such as signal jammers.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: Precisely. Which explains its longevity in the military context.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: Though dealing with the wide network of wires was always a headache for my men...
Even if the mind does not take the form of a tree,
this method is worth attempting if the mind can be ■■■■■ into an arboreal model and interpreted through it.
Is language not the same?
■■ take mere ■■■■■ ■■■■■■■■■■, devoid of meaning, and confine them within the form of language—and through it, ■■ communicate.
I define this invisible, unstable mind as a tree.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Huh, look at the tags. Why are these clothes more expensive than the others?>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: That is because the display you are looking at is for this season's Prêt-à-porter items.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Prêt-à-porter?>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: It refers to made-to-stock, ready-to-wear items; those of higher quality and prestige, in particular.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Prestige but ready-to-wear, huh...>
I take a closer look with Meursault's explanation in mind... But I'm not entirely sure what's supposed to be so prestige and quality about these...
[Prêt-à-porter. Contains 150% of the Golden Yarn compared to the Last Season's!]
Upon closer inspection, I notice that it contains only 0.00015% of the so-called "Golden Yarn." Doesn't seem anywhere near significant enough to warrant putting that on the advertisement.

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: Doesn't this mean that the last season's products had only 0.0001% Golden Yarn...?

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: ... I'm willing to bet that Whale chips from U Corp. have more Whale in them than this has Golden Yarn.
[Origami CollectioN ° 92, 2 of 5.]

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <The ones on the other side at least made small changes between each iteration, but these ones are... Honestly, everything in this "collection" looks the same to me.>

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: Oh, right...! I remember learning about how some prints and sculptures are made with creating multiple identical copies in mind, only giving a different number to each "iteration" to distinguish them.

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: And even though each piece is pretty much indistinguishable from one another, their value might vary depending on the number they're given.

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: That might be what we're looking at here, actually. Maybe there really isn't any difference between each iteration.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: The gaze that pierces an object straight down to its essence, unswayed by its surface-level label... No common person could have noticed such a subtle detail. I expected no less of our Executive Manager!

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... These probably look the same to most people, though...>
<color=#ebcaa2>... Aren't you a busy bee?</color>
The voice snaps me back to reality, and I realize I've been greedily pawing at the inside of the cash drawer.
<color=#ebcaa2>If you're that strapped for eyeballs... Why don't you go help the Mannequins exit the stage?</color>
Shuddering at the subtle contempt in her voice, I slam the cash register shut and quickly leave the scene.
Am I just blindly rummaging through these in hopes of finding a stroke of luck...?

markers.notes: Interact with Arc Floor Lamp after killing him (only possible after advancing to B1F).
Interacting with the couch spawns Drawer enemies.
Interacting with the couch spawns Drawer enemies.
Obtained during the Furniture Hall Quests.

texts.text: Tap tap tap. Swish swish swish. Rhythmic tapping followed by brooms sweeping the floor.
The sound has gotten quieter now, as though it's coming from afar.

texts.speaker: Hong Lu
texts.text: These don't look like artificial plants... Maybe someone's been watering them regularly?

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: The soil is dry. It is likely that this plant is a type that thrives on little to no water— Mm.
Meursault picked something up.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... Why would anyone put that in a plant pot?>

texts.speaker: Don Quixote
texts.text: Hoh? Hast thou never stored aught of great importance within a pot of plant, Manager Esquire?

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <No...? What about you guys?>

texts.speaker: Hong Lu
texts.text: I have. When we were young, Xichun would find pretty rocks and petals and gift them to me. I'd keep those hidden in the flower pots at Yihongyuan.

texts.speaker: Don Quixote
texts.text: Haha... Though this be not a tale of mine, I know that Nicolina had always hidden a key of hers in one of the flower pots decorating the front gates of our castle.

texts.speaker: Don Quixote
texts.text: Oft did I scold her for such carelessness, that a villain might come and snatch the keys for their own ill use... Alas, the key remained secret and safe until the day we tore the castle down.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Do you think that's why they've hidden it here...? For safekeeping?>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: That is unlikely, Manager.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: The inhabitants of the fourth floor would rather decorate themselves with the trinket than keep it hidden.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Then... let's take it with us.>
Meursault picked up 10 eyeballs.
Of the two lamps, the lit one whispers something. Its lampshade silently swings like a pendulum.
Blink.
Blink.
Bliiiiink.
The lamp seems to blink gratefully.
BlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlink
... Not grateful, got it.
■■■■■■ draws like from like, taking the form that provokes the least aversion.
But what we need is not something which is drawn up, but that which blooms.
The bucket must become a seed. It must become a will that bursts forth.
The ■■■■■■■■ human body and its structure are built according to a design inscribed in our very genes.
In the same manner, a blueprint bearing the diagram of the tree must be implanted within people.
... But how?
Perhaps ■■■■■■ should have taken the form of light, not water.
Because to gaze upon something means that the light has entered me.
Because to gaze upon something is to bear its seed beyond any power to resist.

markers.notes: Teleports you to the eastern house.
Teleports you to the western house.

texts.speaker: Le Rouge Porter
texts.text: Should've brought another pair of hands...

texts.speaker: Le Rouge Porter
texts.text: ... Who the hell are you people?

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Are you waiting for something here?>

texts.speaker: Faust
texts.text: We are curious as to what you are awaiting here.

texts.speaker: Le Rouge Porter
texts.text: Need to strip the Hides from B3 and haul 'em back. Don't know why, but supplies haven't been coming through lately—

texts.speaker: Le Rouge Porter
texts.text: ...! Wait. Shh... I can hear the Voice again!
The Rouge porter shoved past us, pressed themself against the wall, and broke into a blissful grin.
The door is blocked. Pressing an ear against it reveals a jumble of noises beyond—voices, footsteps, and more.

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: Well, we're not getting through here, that's for certain. Thing won't even take a scratch.

texts.speaker: Faust
texts.text: It likely leads to another area of B1. Access may become possible once a particular condition is satisfied... but information on the prerequisite is not yet accessible.

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: Huh! Just how huge is this department store...?
<color=#ebcaa2>As vast as a Giant's imagination. That's the kind of place it is.</color>

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <A Giant's imagination...>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: Hmm.

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: Whoa... what's this, a mime routine or something?
Meursault had clearly grasped the knob and moved as though wrenching the door open. Yet the door itself remained exactly where it was.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: The tactile sensation of turning the doorknob and pushing the door open was there.

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: Uh... Maybe your head never closed all the way after the Alterationist opened it upstairs... Manager Bud, how about giving the clock a spin for him?

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: You know, this fella's got a sneaky knack for slapstick.

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: Huh? Well, look at that.
... It would appear that Gregor has just experienced the exact same thing.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Meursault!>

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Are you all right?!>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: I've sustained dermal lacerations, but they are not severe enough to impede me.
As Meursault rises and briskly dusts himself off, I could hear someone—or something—snickering at him.
Something seems to be lurking beyond the window.

Knocked on the door.
Hurried footsteps scurry away at the sound, and then the presence vanishes.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <I think we're being avoided...>
Metal clashes against metal with a heavy clanging.
Through the window, a huge, unidentifiable thing is feeding what looks like hide into a hole in the wall.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <What is it doing...?>

texts.speaker: Faust
texts.text: That aperture is the kind commonly employed for waste disposal in multi-unit residences. It is also referred to as "dust chute."

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: But... isn't this just a detached house?

texts.speaker: Faust
texts.text: That is common sense as established within the City, Herr Gregor. It is difficult to apply the same standard to the way things are in the Symbolic.

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: Huh... you're saying a dust chute isn't a common-sense concept here then...?
... I pull the two Sinners apart before their squabbling can get worse.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Didn't expect to see a door in a place like this.>

texts.speaker: Faust
texts.text: Given where it faces, opening it has a high probability of connecting us to the Food Hall...

texts.speaker: Faust
texts.text: ... Though the available evidence is insufficient to be absolutely certain.
The door opens onto an empty space drowned in darkness.

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: Uh... We're not going in there, are we, Manager Bud?

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... Let's take the corridor. Might be safer that way.>

markers.notes: Sous Chef while retrieving the Ruminations of the Prey

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: Sous Chef. I have a question.

texts.speaker: Sous Chef
texts.text: W-what is it, you hear?

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: I want to know what form the Ruminations of the Prey take and by what criteria they may be identified.

texts.speaker: Sous Chef
texts.text: I don't know, you hear?

texts.speaker: Faust
texts.text: We intend to contribute to the Meat Soda. Your guidance would be appreciated.

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: Hey... Soup Chef.

texts.speaker: Sous Chef
texts.text: I don't know, you hear?! I don't know!

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: Good grief... *puff* All right, "Sous Chef."

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: How're we supposed to get you that Ruminations thing if you won't even tell us what it looks like? Come on, we're trying to make a "contribution" here—you're the Sous Chef, aren't you? Act like one.

texts.speaker: Sous Chef
texts.text: The buggy buggy arm would be perfect... but the Meat Soda matters more for everyone's sake, you hear? I'll answer because I'm a good, responsible Sous Chef, you hear?

texts.speaker: Sous Chef
texts.text: The Ruminations of the Prey hang at the far left, you hear? They dangle-dongle, you hear? Something glitters between the ribs, you hear?

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... Then we should look for a cut of meat with the Golden Hide attached.>

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: Oh? You could've told us from the start, you know. Would've saved us both a lot of trouble.

texts.speaker: Sous Chef
texts.text: Wondering if you don't hate that arm, you hear?

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: ... I do hate it. Like you wouldn't believe it. I don't go a day without wanting to rip it clean off my body.

texts.speaker: Sous Chef
texts.text: That you can just contribute, you hear? Wondering why you wouldn't, you hear?

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: Sometimes, Sous Chef... there are things that stick to you no matter how much you hate them, you hear?

texts.speaker: Sous Chef
texts.text: I still want it... But if that's so, cherish it, you hear? Now I must go, you hear? You're not the only one who's busy, you hear?

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Oh, wow.>

texts.speaker: Faust
texts.text: You transitioned between persuasion and intimidation with notable fluency, Gregor. Faust must admit that Faust has learned something today.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: It was an exceptionally effective method.

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: Eh... Since when did you start giving me compliments like that, fellas? ... Ahem. Anyhow... Let's get moving.
Therapy or conversation cannot heal the soul.
Measured against this schema, psychotherapy is no more than a ■■■■■■■■■ ■■■■■■■.
But now that I know the shape of the human mind, could I not diagnose and heal it?
If so, it may be possible to heal not only ■ ■■■■., where I was born, but also the terrible suffering that has enveloped the City itself.
It may be possible to heal the people of the City who are afflicted by an illness that makes them unable to know who they are ■■ ■■■■■ ■■■■■■■ toward death.

markers.name: King of Needleworks
markers.notes: Fought as part of the story.
Obtained when speaking to B2F Floor Manager after defeating King of Needleworks.

texts.text: The machine looks complicated to operate.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Meursault, do you know how to operate this?>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: I am not familiar with the work procedures of Sisyphe's lower floors.
Meanwhile, Outis began manipulating the machine's complex display.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: Hm... I do not yet understand the operating principle, but I have a general grasp of the structure.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Oh, wow...>

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: The interface presents three functions: extraction, spinning, and dyeing. Your orders, Executive Manager?
Three buttons appear on the display Outis indicates.
With a disconcerting whir, the machine sucked a patch of Meursault's skin onto its surface.

texts.speaker: Ryōshū
texts.text: Huh. These threads are O. of a K.
With a disconcerting whir, the machine sucked a patch of Meursault's skin onto its surface.
With a disconcerting whir, the machine sucked a patch of Meursault's skin onto its surface.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: ... Are... you going to press it again, Executive Manager?
With a disconcerting whir, the machine sucked a patch of Meursault's skin onto its surface.

texts.speaker: Ryōshū
texts.text: You want it S.I.T.?

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: She is asking whether your objective is to have the skin "split into threads," Manager.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <N-no, that's not what I'm doing... But has Sinclair ever interpreted that one before?>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: He has interpreted "S.E.N.I.T." before on the bus. It stands for "split every nerve into threads."

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <I really don't remember what the context was when she said it.>
A spool of thread plopped out of the contraption.
It appears to be thread made from... Meursault's skin.
There shouldn't be any reason to press this button again.
The threads twang lightly as the machine pulls them tight.
They're starting to multiply...

texts.speaker: Needlekin Laborer
texts.text: ... Uh, we weren't told anything about increased production volume.

texts.speaker: Needlekin Laborer 2
texts.text: Don't you think you're going a little too fast? Slow down with the threads over there!
... The customers working nearby are glaring daggers at us.
... The accusatory glares around me are too sharp to risk pressing it again.
A warning states that no dye is available.
Nothing happened.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: With all due respect, Executive Manager... may I ask what exactly it is that you intend to accomplish?

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... I mean... Sometimes you just want to mash some buttons, right?>
As I try to hammer the button once more, something taps my elbow.
I turned to find Ryōshū's scabbard, Araya.
For a moment, I could swear I heard it say, "You really should stop acting like a kid..."
Yeah, I should stop. This is getting ridiculous.
A sound resembling the rumble of a train comes from beyond the door.
As I move closer to investigate, the light leaking through the gap grows steadily brighter.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Aaargh!!>

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: ...! Executive Manager!

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: Are you unharmed?! What did you see?

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <I heard something like a train... and then this huge flash of light came through...>
Outis scrutinizes every inch of the gap, then points as though she has found something.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: Something is lodged inside. Meursault, can you remove it?

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: I can.
Meursault removes an eyeball from the gap.
A sofa painted in a riot of colors.
Whenever I try to sit, the person beside Palette fixes me with a vicious glare.
Ryōshū levels her with a reciprocative glare of her own. Her scabbard sways behind her. Somehow, the motion seems like the wave of a hand of someone trying to stop a fight.
The shape of this tree is but an outcome of compiling my ■■■■■■■■ discoveries; I did not prescribe this form.
Just as the human body has an ■■■■■■■■■■ diagram, this tree is a diagram of the human mind.
To treat the afflicted, one must first understand the body.
Yet no one has thus far completed a visualization of the human soul—or consciousness—let alone devised the means of systematizing its structure.
